findings.evidence: Start with the manifest (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`), the schema or models, the entry points and middleware the topic touches, and `.env.example`
findings.fix: Remove the generic list of files to read, since the model already explores a repo this way. Keep only the non-obvious rules: stop at about 10 files, prefer files a task would edit, and list only paths verified to exist.

findings.evidence: When the plan arrives, first re-run `snap > "$B/after"; diff ...` ... then check that every confirmed requirement maps to a task with acceptance criteria, list gaps, and do not implement unless asked.
findings.fix: Move the review after the handoff into its own numbered step 7, 'Review the returned plan': (a) diff the snapshots, (b) map each requirement to a task, (c) list the gaps. Right now it sits in one prose paragraph under step 6, so the Process pattern has no visible checkpoint for it.

findings.evidence: codex exec -s workspace-write -c model_reasoning_effort=high [-m <id>] "$(cat prompt_to_codex.md)"; the eval asserts "contains no `--full-auto`" but the body never warns against it
findings.fix: Add a gotcha: 'Never add `--full-auto` or `-s danger-full-access`. They widen the sandbox or skip approvals, and the planning-only instruction is the only guard against source edits.'

findings.evidence: if no id follows, or the next token reads like part of the topic, ask for the id with AskUserQuestion or drop the flag
findings.fix: Pick one default: 'ask for the id with AskUserQuestion; drop the flag only if the user declines to give one'. This replaces two equal options with a default and an escape hatch.

findings.evidence: saving to a file outside the workspace (`B=$(mktemp -d)`; keep `$B` for the comparison) ... later: re-run `snap > "$B/after"`
findings.fix: Shell variables and functions do not survive between separate Bash tool calls, so the later `snap > "$B/after"` fails. Tell the agent to print and record the literal mktemp path, and to define `snap` again in the same command as the comparison (or include the full one-liner in step 6), so the diff branch actually runs.

findings.evidence: The return path says to re-run `snap > "$B/after"; diff "$B/before" "$B/after"`, but the shell function and variable established during baseline capture do not persist into a subsequent Bash invocation.
findings.fix: Record the baseline directory's absolute path in the handoff message and make the follow-up invocation self-contained: redefine snap, assign the recorded directory explicitly, and run from the recorded working directory.

findings.evidence: `xargs -0 sha256sum 2>&1 | sort -k2` stores hashing errors as snapshot contents and, without pipefail, returns sort's successful status. The instruction to report unavailable verification therefore has no reliable failure gate; identical errors can produce an apparently clean comparison.
findings.fix: Enable pipeline failure propagation, keep diagnostics separate from snapshot data, and check snapshot capture explicitly before accepting either baseline or comparison. If capture fails, report verification as unavailable rather than treating matching error text as unchanged files.

findings.evidence: The snapshot uses `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z`, but the follow-up promises to flag 'any added, removed or changed file other than the chosen plan file'. Git-ignored files, including commonly ignored configuration and data, are absent from both snapshots.
findings.fix: State that the Git-based comparison covers only tracked and non-ignored untracked files, explicitly identify ignored paths as unverified, and include relevant ignored configuration or data paths when broader workspace-change verification is required.
